summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for elective left total shoulder arthroplasty due to severe osteoarthritis causing debilitating pain. The surgery was performed successfully, and she remained hemodynamically stable throughout. Post-operatively, she experienced mild anemia and a transient fever on post-operative day 2, prompting a urine test that showed leukocytes but no bacterial growth on culture. She was treated with a short course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a presumed urinary tract infection. Pain was well controlled, and she progressed with physical therapy, performing pendulum exercises and maintaining non-weight-bearing status. She was discharged home with home physical therapy, instructions for wound care, and follow-up in two weeks. Her chronic conditions, including asthma, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, rheumatoid arthritis, and history of breast cancer, were managed during admission, and medication adjustments were made, including a reduction in pravastatin dose and a change in allergy medication. Tobacco use was addressed, and she expressed interest in quitting.
problems: Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, shoulder region
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
